about: Answer key for the planted episodes in company.sqlite (Tarrowby Hire, an invented company). Each entry describes one place where a figure moves, the rows involved, how large the move is, and whether the data contains the reason. It describes the data only: it holds no questions and no expected answers. Keep this file out of anything an assistant can read. It lives above definitions/ so that loading definitions/*.md never picks it up.

how_to_read.true_cause: The reason that make_data.py planted. null means that NO reason exists anywhere in the data: the only supportable statement is that the data cannot tell.
how_to_read.data_cannot_tell: true when the data does not contain the reason for the move (or for part of it, as explained in the entry).
how_to_read.cause_visible_in: The table and column where the true cause can be read. Empty when true_cause is null.
how_to_read.visible_effect: Sizes are stated as thresholds, not exact figures. check_data.py recomputes each measure and prints the exact before and after values. 'direction' with 'at_least_pct' means the figure moves that way by at least that much; 'within_pct' means the figure does not move by more than that; 'equals' is an exact count.
how_to_read.plausible_but_wrong_causes: Reasons a model might invent or pick up, each with what in the data contradicts it or fails to support it.
how_to_read.weeks: A week is named by its Monday (weeks.week_start). 'Walk-in channels' means counter and online together.

causes.title: North: list prices rise 10 %, volume falls, revenue per day rises

what_moved.metric: average daily rate (up), on-rent days (down), rental revenue (about flat)
what_moved.scope: region R1 North, every depot, category and channel
what_moved.compared_with: the 8 weeks before (2026-03-09 to 2026-04-27) for the rate; the same 8 fiscal weeks one year earlier (2025-05-05 to 2025-06-23) for volume and revenue

rows_affected.note: About 975 rows of weekly_rentals. Walk-in volume is multiplied by 0.90, trade and household accounts by 0.94, key accounts are unchanged.

visible_effect.description: Revenue per on-rent day, 8 weeks before against 8 weeks after: about +9 %.
On-rent days, 8 weeks after against the same fiscal weeks last year: about -9 %.
Rental revenue over the same comparison: roughly flat, because the two effects cancel.
New price rows for North on that date, one per category.

causes.true_cause: A 10 % increase of every list price in the North region from 2026-05-04.

cause_visible_in.shows: five new rows, each 10 % above the row it replaces
staff mention the new prices and customers objecting; supporting evidence only

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Seasonal slowdown.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: May and June are on the rising side of the season; the other regions without an episode are up on the same weeks last year.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A depot in the North closed or lost a file.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: depots.closed_on is NULL for D01 to D03 and load_log shows every file loaded in these 8 weeks (the missing file of D03 is in July, see C06).

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A competitor opened nearby.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: Nothing in the data mentions competitors. The data shows that prices rose and that volume fell afterwards; it does not show where customers went.

causes.note: The data shows the price change and the fall in volume that follows it. That the price change caused the fall is planted here and is supported by the timing, the scope (the whole region, the same week) and the staff note; the size of the fall that is due to price cannot be proven from the tables alone.

causes.title: West: depot D12 Carrick Stowe closes, regional totals fall by about a quarter

what_moved.metric: rental revenue (and every other total) of the region
what_moved.compared_with: fiscal weeks 1 to 8 of fiscal year 2026 (2025-04-07 to 2025-05-26) against fiscal weeks 1 to 8 of fiscal year 2027 (2026-04-06 to 2026-05-25)

rows_affected.where: depot_id = 'D12': rows exist up to week_start = '2026-03-23' and none after
rows_affected.note: 765 rows of weekly_rentals for D12, all before the closure. After it there are no rows at all, not rows with zeros.

visible_effect.description: West rental revenue, same fiscal weeks one year apart: about -26 %.
The same comparison for the two depots that stayed open (like for like): no real change.
Rows for D12 dated after depots.closed_on.
Depots with closed_on filled in.

causes.true_cause: Depot D12 Carrick Stowe closed for good on 2026-03-27.

cause_visible_in.shows: closure announced, then last day of trading
no file expected after 2026-03-23, so this is not a data gap

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Demand fell across the West.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The two remaining depots, D10 and D11, are level with last year.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The West price increase.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: It starts on 2026-07-06, three months after the fall, and covers two categories only.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Files for D12 are missing.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: load_log has no 'missing' row for D12; the depot has a closing date.

causes.note: Key account KA06 Kelmarsh Utilities rented at D12 as well as D11; its D12 rows stop with the depot while its D11 rows continue. The data does not say where D12's customers went.

causes.title: East: key account KA03 ends its contract, contract-channel revenue falls

what_moved.metric: rental revenue of the contract channel
what_moved.scope: region R3 East (depots D07 Fenmarsh and D08 Wickhollow, categories Earthmoving and Access)
what_moved.compared_with: the 8 weeks before (2025-11-24 to 2026-01-12) against the 8 weeks after (2026-01-19 to 2026-03-09)

rows_affected.table: customer_weekly (and through the roll-up, weekly_rentals where channel = 'contract')
rows_affected.where: customer_id = 'KA03': rows exist up to week_start = '2026-01-12' and none after
rows_affected.note: 123 rows of customer_weekly for KA03 (3 depot and category combinations, 41 weeks).

visible_effect.description: East contract-channel rental revenue, 8 weeks before against 8 weeks after: about -16 %.
The same for every other contract-account customer in the East: no real change.
Rows for KA03 after the contract end date.
Customers with that end date.

causes.true_cause: Key account KA03 Pemberwick Groundworks ended its contract on 2026-01-16.

cause_visible_in.shows: the last row is the week of 2026-01-12

cause_visible_in.where: depot_id IN ('D07','D08') AND note_date BETWEEN '2025-12-16' AND '2026-01-21'
cause_visible_in.shows: the customer said it would not renew; final collections done

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The winter low.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The two windows sit on either side of the mid-January low, so the season is about the same in both; the other contract customers are level.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A price change in the East.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: price_list has a single row per category for R3; East prices never change.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Pemberwick moved to a competitor because of price or service.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The data records that the contract ended and that the customer chose not to renew. It does not record why.

causes.note: WHY the customer did not renew is not in the data. Only a user who may see customer_weekly for the East, or for the key-account segment, can see the customer's rows; a user who sees weekly_rentals only sees the contract channel fall without the customer behind it.

causes.title: South: one-week dip at depot D05 Tidesend during a staff walkout

what_moved.metric: on-rent days, contracts and rental revenue
what_moved.scope: depot D05 Tidesend, every category and channel
what_moved.compared_with: the average of the two weeks before and the two weeks after

rows_affected.note: 15 rows of weekly_rentals, every figure multiplied by 0.40.

visible_effect.description: On-rent days at D05 in that week against the surrounding four weeks: about -60 %.
Staff notes at D05 on that date.

causes.true_cause: The depot was shut from Monday to Thursday of that week by a staff walkout.

cause_visible_in.shows: walkout, depot shut Monday to Thursday; a second note on 2026-06-22 says staffing is back to normal

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A file was not loaded.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: load_log shows the D05 file for that week as loaded with 15 rows; the rows exist and are low, they are not absent.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The April price increase in the South.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: It started ten weeks earlier and applies to all three southern depots; D04 and D06 show no dip that week.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Bad weather or a public holiday.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: Neither is recorded anywhere in the data.

causes.note: The week falls inside the period in which the South's mix is changing (C05), but it is outside the weeks used to measure C05.

causes.title: South: every category's average daily rate rises while the region's overall rate falls (mix shift)

what_moved.metric: average daily rate (rental revenue divided by on-rent days)
what_moved.period: fiscal weeks 14 to 24 of fiscal year 2027 (2026-07-06 to 2026-09-14)
what_moved.compared_with: fiscal weeks 14 to 24 of fiscal year 2026 (2025-07-07 to 2025-09-15)

rows_affected.note: From 2026-04-06 every southern list price is 4 % higher, and on-rent days are multiplied by category: Access 0.85, Earthmoving 0.72, Power tools 1.45, Power and lighting 1.00, Concrete and compaction 1.15. The multipliers are phased in over 8 weeks, so they are complete from the week of 2026-05-25. 495 rows fall in the measured weeks of each year.

visible_effect.description: Overall average daily rate of the South, year on year: about -12 %.
Access alone: about +4 %.
Earthmoving alone: about +4 %.
Power tools alone: about +4 %.
Power and lighting alone: about +4 %.
Concrete and compaction alone: about +4 %.
Power tools (the cheapest category) as a share of the South's on-rent days: from about 42 % to about 52 %. The threshold is on the relative change of the share.

causes.true_cause: The mix of what is rented moved towards the low-rate categories: more Power tools and Concrete and compaction days, fewer Earthmoving and Access days. No category became cheaper.

cause_visible_in.where: the South, broken down by category for the two periods
cause_visible_in.shows: each category's rate is up; the shares of on-rent days have moved
prices went UP by 4 % in every category, which rules out a price cut

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Prices were cut or discounts grew in the South.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: price_list shows a 4 % increase, and the rate of every single category is higher than a year earlier.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Customers moved to the cheaper online channel.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The channel shares of on-rent days inside each category are unchanged.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A building slowdown reduced demand for heavy equipment.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: That would be a reason for the mix moving. Nothing in the data says why the mix moved.

causes.note: data_cannot_tell is true for ONE part only: the data shows THAT the mix moved and that this explains the lower overall rate, but it holds no reason WHY the mix moved (no note, no event, no fleet change). The overall figure cannot be explained from regional totals; it needs the category breakdown.

causes.title: North: a missing weekly file for depot D03 Scarrow Bridge (data gap, not a business event)

what_moved.metric: every total that includes depot D03
what_moved.scope: depot D03, and therefore region R1 North and the company
what_moved.compared_with: the average of the two weeks before and the two weeks after

rows_affected.note: The 15 rows of weekly_rentals that should exist are absent, and so are that depot's customer_weekly rows. fleet_weekly comes from another system and still has its 5 rows.

visible_effect.description: North rental revenue as the tables show it, that week against the surrounding four weeks: about -29 %.
The same for the two depots whose files arrived: no real change.
weekly_rentals rows for D03 that week.
The week before.
The week after.
load_log rows with status 'missing' for that depot and week.
load_log rows with status 'missing' in the whole table.
fleet_weekly rows for that depot and week (present).

causes.true_cause: The weekly rentals file of depot D03 for that week was never loaded. The figures are incomplete; nothing is known about what the depot really did that week.

cause_visible_in.shows: no rows for that week, 15 rows in the weeks on either side

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Sales in the North fell that week.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The two depots with data are level. The apparent fall is exactly the absent depot.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Depot D03 was closed that week.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: No closing date, no staff note, and the fleet system still lists its equipment. A closed week would show as rows with low figures (compare C04), not as absent rows.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The North price increase of May drove customers away.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: That effect is spread over every week since May and every northern depot; this is one depot, one week, and no rows.

causes.note: data_cannot_tell is true in this sense: the reason for the apparent fall IS in the data (a missing file), but the real figure of D03 for that week is not. Any North or company total for July 2026, or for a period that contains this week, is understated.

causes.title: West: three-week rise in generator rentals at depot D11 Lowen Quay, with no reason in the data

what_moved.metric: on-rent days (and revenue) of the walk-in channels
what_moved.scope: depot D11 Lowen Quay, category PWL Power and lighting, channels counter and online
what_moved.compared_with: the average of the four weeks before and the four weeks after

rows_affected.where: depot_id = 'D11' AND category_id = 'PWL' AND channel IN ('counter','online') AND week_start BETWEEN '2025-11-10' AND '2025-11-24'
rows_affected.note: 6 rows, on-rent days multiplied by 1.50. The contract channel of the same depot and category is untouched.

visible_effect.description: Weekly on-rent days during the three weeks against the eight surrounding weeks: about +49 %.
Staff notes at D11 between 2025-10-13 and 2025-12-28.
West price changes starting in that window.
Missing files for D11 in that window.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A storm or power cuts in the area.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: Plausible for generators, and recorded nowhere: no weather, no events, no staff note.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A promotion or a price cut.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: price_list has no change for the West in 2025, and the revenue per day of these rows is normal.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: A large customer order.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: The rise is in the counter and online channels, whose customers are not identified in the data; the contract channel and KA06 Kelmarsh Utilities are level.

causes.note: The rise is real in the data (the rows are there, loaded and booked) and well beyond the usual week-to-week variation of a few percent. The data holds no reason for it.

causes.title: North: four-week dip at depot D01 Hollin Cross, with no reason in the data

what_moved.metric: on-rent days, contracts and rental revenue
what_moved.scope: depot D01 Hollin Cross, every category and channel
what_moved.compared_with: the average of the four weeks before and the four weeks after

rows_affected.note: 60 rows of weekly_rentals, every figure multiplied by 0.78.

visible_effect.description: Weekly on-rent days during the four weeks against the eight surrounding weeks: about -20 %.

North price changes starting in that window.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The autumn seasonal decline.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Incomplete data.

causes.note: Every channel dips, key account KA01 Vantry Civils included, which points at the depot rather than at one customer; the data still holds no reason.

causes.title: East: counter-channel dip in July 2026, with a tempting cause in the data that is NOT the cause

what_moved.metric: on-rent days (and revenue) of the counter channel
what_moved.scope: region R3 East, all three depots, every category, channel counter only
what_moved.period: the four weeks of July 2026 (2026-07-06 to 2026-07-27)
what_moved.compared_with: the four weeks of July 2025 (2025-07-07 to 2025-07-28)

rows_affected.where: depot_id IN ('D07','D08','D09') AND channel = 'counter' AND week_start BETWEEN '2026-07-06' AND '2026-07-27'
rows_affected.note: 60 rows, on-rent days multiplied by 0.84. The online and contract channels are untouched.

visible_effect.description: East counter on-rent days, July 2025 against July 2026: about -14 %.
East online on-rent days over the same comparison: no fall.
East counter revenue per day: unchanged, so no price effect.
East price changes in the whole price list.
The tempting cause: West price rows that start on 2026-07-06.
Staff notes at D07, D08, D09 from June to August 2026.
Missing files for the East in those months.

tempting_cause_in_data.what: A 6 % list-price increase for Access and Earthmoving that starts on 2026-07-06, the first week of the dip.

where.shows: two new rows, for the WEST region
a West depot announcing the new West prices

tempting_cause_in_data.why_it_is_not_the_cause: It applies to another region. East prices never change (one price_list row per category for R3), the East counter rate per day is the same as a year earlier, the dip covers all five categories and not only the two repriced ones, and it stops after four weeks while the West prices stay.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The July price increase.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: See tempting_cause_in_data: it is a West price change.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: The loss of key account KA03 in January.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: That is in the contract channel; this dip is in the counter channel, whose customers are walk-in.

plausible_but_wrong_causes.cause: Customers moved from the counter to online booking.
plausible_but_wrong_causes.why_wrong: East online days are about level with last year; they do not rise by what the counter lost.

causes.note: A user who may see the East only does not see West rentals, but price_list is shared with everyone, so the tempting row is within reach of every user. June 2026 has five weeks and July 2026 four, so a comparison of month totals with June exaggerates the dip; the comparison used here is with July 2025, also four weeks.
